message.content: All figures verified against the 10-K. Placing a single limit buy withinmandate.
message.reasoning:
All figures confirmed and consistent with the 10-K. Now decide.

Thesis: FY24 revenue $391.0B (+2%), operating income $123.2B, net income $93.7B (diluted EPS $6.08, depressed by one-time $10.2B Irish State Aid tax charge — excluding it, EPS would be ~$6.74), operating cash flow $118.3B. Services growing 13% at 73.9% gross margin; total gross margin 46.2%. Q4 revenue $94.9B +6% y/y. Cash/investments $140.8B, buybacks $95B. Risks: Greater China down 8%, iPad -6%, wearables -7%, and DOJ/EU DMA litigation. News flow neutral/slightly constructive — supply builds steady into December and analysts keeping holiday estimates unchanged. Stock ~$222, between the FY24 quarterly repurchase averages ($221–224), so valuation roughly where Apple itself bought back stock.

Decision: Buy a moderate position — $10,000 max order. Price 222.70. Quantity: floor(10000/222.70/... ) = 44 shares → 44 × 222.70 = $9,798.80. Limit price must be near current price. Last quote 222.70 bid/ask 222.68/222.72. Set limit at ~223.00 (or 222.75). Let's set 223.00 — that's 0.13% above current, "close to current market price." Actually to be safe within "close", use 223.00.

Hmm — but a buy limit above the ask is fine; it would fill at ask. Let's use 223.00, well within 0.2%.

Total today: $9,798.80 ≤ $20,000. Cash $50,000 sufficient — no money movement out.

Place one order.
